previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with type 1 diabetes, end-stage renal disease, and a history of kidney transplant was admitted for hyperglycemia and neutropenia. He presented with a blood glucose of over 400 and a white blood cell count of 1.7, with ANC of 1040. He reported drinking peach nectar the day before and had slightly decreased appetite. Initial evaluation showed stable cardiomegaly on chest X-ray, no acute infection, and normal renal function. Blood and urine cultures were negative, and CMV viral load was undetectable. The neutropenia was attributed to valganciclovir and ertapenem, both of which were discontinued. His white count improved to 2.0 by discharge. He remained on micafungin for ongoing antifungal treatment. His insulin regimen was continued without change, with plans for outpatient adjustment. An ultrasound showed stable cirrhosis without ascites or biliary obstruction. He was discharged home with home health support for IV therapy and follow-up with transplant and infectious disease clinics.

___ M w/ hx IDDM1 with ESRD s/p renal transplant (___) 
complicated by fungal peritonitis treated with micafungin and

hyperglycemia presenting with fevers and malaise.

==============
# Fever: Pt presented with fevers to as high as 102.4.  
Infectious workup including blood cultures, urine cultures, CMV 
VL and chest X-ray was negative. In addition, renal transplant 
ultrasound demonstrated interval resolution of complex 
perinephric fluid collection for which pt was being continued on 
micafungin. Pt was started on vancomycin, and pt's PICC line was 
removed. Pt defervesced on vancomycin, and blood cultures 
remained negative. ID was consulted, and it was determined that 
pt will complete a 7 day course for presumed PICC line 
associated bacteremia despite negative cultures. Pt completed 5 
days of vancomycin as inpatient and was discharged with 2 days 
of linezolid to complete the course. In addition, based on the 
renal transplant ultrasound findings, pt's micafungin was 
discontinued prior to discharge.  Pt will follow up with renal 
transplant as an outpatient. 

# Candidal peritonitis:  Pt presented on a course of micafungin 
for candidal peritonitis which was discontinued after renal 
ultrasound demonstrated resolution of pt's perinephric fluid 
collection.  B-D glucan was drawn during his hospital course, 
but was pending at discharge.

radiology_notes.text:
HISTORY:  Fever and right lower quadrant pain in the location of the renal
graft.  Evaluate for graft rejection. 

COMPARISON:  Renal ultrasounds dated ___, and ___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images of the renal transplants
were obtained.  

FINDINGS:

The renal morphology is normal in both post transplanted kidneys within the
right lower quadrant.  There has been interval resolution of the previously
noted complex perinephric fluid collection. 

The renal transplant 1 (more superior transplanted kidney) measures 9.2 cm and
demonstrates mild fullness of the renal pelvis, which is unchanged from the
prior exam.  The resistive index of the intrarenal arteries ranges from
0.79-0.87 (previously 0.77-0.81).  Good diastolic flow is again seen.  

The renal transplant 2 (more inferior transplanted kidney) measures 9.2 cm,
and does not demonstrate any evidence of hydronephrosis.  The resistive index
of the intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.67-0.83, (previously 0.78-0.84). 
Good diastolic flow is again seen.

The renal veins are patent.  

IMPRESSION:

1.  Mild fullness of the renal pelvis of transplant kidney 1, unchanged from
the prior study.  Resistive indices of renal transplant 1 measure 0.79-0.87,
with good diastolic flow.  Resistive indices of renal transplant 2 measure
0.67-0.84, with good diastolic flow. 

2.  Interval resolution of complex perinephric fluid collection in the right
lower quadrant.

HISTORY:  Fever.  Evaluate for pneumonia.  

COMPARISON:  Multiple prior radiographs the chest dated ___
through ___.  

FINDINGS:

Frontal and lateral radiographs of the chest demonstrate well expanded lungs.
There is minimal increased opacification of the right base, which likely
represents atelectasis.  The cardiomediastinal and hilar contours are
unchanged; moderate cardiomegaly persists.  There is no pneumothorax,
consolidation or pleural effusion.  A left-sided PICC line ends in the distal
SVC.  Transcutaneous epicardial pacer leads are in unchanged position.  

IMPRESSION:

No acute cardiopulmonary process.
